newsitem.title: CHINA: Air India offers discounted HK-Seoul cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Air India offers discounted HK-Seoul cargo rates.

text.p: Air India is offering discounted bellyhold cargo rates to try and build market share on its new Hong Kong-Seoul route, said its Hong Kong cargo manager, Kevin Fung,
The Indian flag carrier now operates five flights a week between Bombay and Hong Kong, four of them continuing on to either the South Korean capital or Osaka, Japan.
Since the beginning of July, Air India has extended two of its three Airbus A310 flights a week between Bombay and Hong Kong on to Seoul.

"We are more than happy with the results so far to Seoul. Most of the cargo we are flying to Seoul is destined for America. Depending on passenger load, we have about five tonnes of bellyhold cargo space," Fung said.
"Because it is a new route, we are offering a 50 HK cents per kg rate reduction (to try and build market share)," he added.
Air India also operates a twice-weekly service between Bombay and Osaka via Hong Kong.
The Wednesday service utilises a Boeing 747-200 passenger aircraft and the Sunday flight a 747-300 Combi aircraft with around 50 tonnes' cargo capacity.
Like other carriers operating to Japan, the weak yen has depressed demand.

"The market between Hong Kong and Japan is not that good and we have lots of competition from the major carriers (such as Cathay Pacific and Japan Airlines which offer higher frequencies). But between Hong Kong and India, loads are more than satisfactory in both directions. Growth is steady," Fung told Reuters.
Fung said the Combi was recruited especially because of high cargo demand between Osaka and India. 90 percent of space is usually taken by ex Japan cargo.

"Ex-Osaka, loads are doing extremely well which is why they requested the Combi. Japanese exporters have lots of machine parts and electrical items and high density shipments, which mean good yields for the airlines," Fung said.
